message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States (sorted roughly by passenger traffic and overall importance):

| Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport | Atlanta, GA | ATL | Largest airport by passenger traffic in the world; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and the Pacific; one of the busiest airports on the West Coast. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport | Chicago, IL | ORD | One of the oldest major hubs; key connecting point for United Airlines and American Airlines. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | Largest airport in the U.S. by land area; major hub for American Airlines. |
| Denver International Airport | Denver, CO | DEN | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; major hub for United Airlines and Southwest Airlines. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport | New York City, NY | JFK | Primary international gateway for the East Coast; major hub for JetBlue and Delta. |
| San Francisco International Airport | San Francisco, CA | SFO | Key hub for United Airlines and a major gateway to Asia. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport | Seattle, WA | SEA | Major hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| Miami International Airport | Miami, FL | MIA | Major hub for LATAM and a key gateway to Latin America. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport | Phoenix, AZ | PHX | Major hub for American Airlines; high volume of domestic flights. |
| Charlotte Douglas International Airport | Charlotte, NC | CLT | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the fastest‑growing airports in the U.S. |
| Orlando International Airport | Orlando, FL | ORL | Major hub for Southwest Airlines; serves a huge leisure travel market. |
| Newark Liberty International Airport | Newark, NJ | EWR | Major hub for United Airlines; primary international gateway for the New York metropolitan area. |
| Washington Dulles International Airport | Dulles, VA | IAD | Major hub for United Airlines; key airport for the Washington, D.C. region. |

These airports are among the busiest in terms of passenger numbers, flight operations, and cargo throughput, and they serve as major hubs for the largest U.S. carriers.
